idea_name: DoC latent z excluding environmental stochasticity
mechanism: Dichotomy of Control replaces Decision Transformer return-to-go with a latent z(τ) trained under a mutual-information constraint so z carries no information about future Rt and St+1 unknown at history time; contrastive training plus Lagrange objective separates policy-controllable factors from environment noise, then policy conditions on z.
data_needed: Offline trajectories of states (OHLC+RSI/CCI/ATR/MACD+volume), account features, prior actions, and realized rewards; RTG model outputting z; Agent conditioned on z
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train Jan–Jul 2023; test Aug 2023; sparse MH attention HistoryBars stack
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a sequence latent that is explicitly denoised of uncontrollable market noise—z itself is a sensor of what the agent can still steer versus stochastic regime residue.
quote: The key observation of the method authors is that z should not contain information related to environmental stochasticity. It should not include information about the future Rt and St+1, which is unknown at the time of the previous history.

idea_name: FQF quantile latent as joint prior and value for RTG
mechanism: Instead of sampling many z~p(z|s0) and ranking by V(z), one FQF (fully parameterized quantile function) layer at the RTG model output jointly represents the prior distribution over latent designations and their expected reward quantiles, so a single forward pass yields a latent that already balances probability and magnitude of reward under stochasticity.
data_needed: Autoregressive RTG inputs: BarDescr×NBarInPattern + account + time embeddings + prior actions; FQF with NRewards outputs and 32 quantiles; no separate V(z) network
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; DoC Research/Study/Test EAs; NRewards-dimensional FQF output fed into Agent
why_new_for_mis: Turns expected-reward designation into a distributional sensor—MIS can read quantile mass over latent returns as a probabilistic regime/edge reading without batch sampling.
quote: Let's recall the fully parameterized quantile function (FQF). It allows you to combine probability and quantitative distributions. This is what we will use in the latent representation generation model.

idea_name: Fixed pre-event entry to avoid news illiquidity
mechanism: Locks trade entry to a fixed Pre_S30=30s before calendar release instead of configurable 5s-or-less windows, because liquidity collapses as high-impact events approach—raising slippage, widening spreads, and producing off-quotes; earlier fixed schedule also cuts backtest tick checks to 30s intervals.
data_needed: Economic calendar event timestamps; PRESECONDLY enum; broker quotes/spread around release
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: News EA context (NFP and high-impact releases); second-level pre-event timing; symbol-agnostic calendar
why_new_for_mis: Frames seconds-to-release as an explicit liquidity clock MIS can monitor—illiquidity risk rises monotonically into the print, independent of directional forecast.
quote: Another factor which should be considered is liquidity. The closer we get to a high-impact news event the more the affected asset becomes illiquid.

mechanism: Loads all same-day calendar events once into memory, partitions them into 24 CArrayObj hour buckets (CTimeByHour/CTimeByDay), then retrieves only the current hour (and minute filter) via switch—so the live event set is a sparse temporal index rather than a full-day scan.
data_needed: In-memory daily Calendar array; HOURLY/MINUTELY enums; SetmyTime/GetmyTime hour–minute filters
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol with MQL5 economic calendar; daily load, hourly/minute retrieval; NFP 14:30 case study
why_new_for_mis: Provides MIS a cheap intra-day event-density sensor: non-empty hour buckets and minute hits are a calendar-regime reading of when news risk is locally active.
quote: a simple solution to this problem would be to at least separate the array into different hours of the day and the expert will only iterate through the array with the matching hour of the current time.

idea_name: Session-boundary overnight liquidity and gap gate
mechanism: CSessions reads SymbolInfoSessionTrade windows, applies hour/minute offsets (default end offset 45 min), and forces flat before session end because overnight books have lower liquidity, wider spreads, slippage, open gaps that skip stops, and swap costs—explicitly treating session edge as a risk regime change.
data_needed: Symbol session schedule via SymbolInfoSessionTrade; server time; offsethour/offsetmin; CloseTrades near SessionEnd
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Symbol session times (broker-dependent); news EA on FX pairs; close 45 min before session end
why_new_for_mis: Turns exchange session calendars into a binary liquidity/gap regime sensor MIS can gate on without estimating vol from ticks.
quote: Liquidity tends to be lower during overnight trading sessions because fewer market participants are active. This can lead to: Wider spreads ... Slippage ... Difficulty closing large positions.

idea_name: Dual stop-order breakout commitment around news
mechanism: Places buy-stop above and sell-stop below pre-news price (straddle); fill of one side is treated as market commitment to a breakout direction, after which FundamentalMode deletes the opposite pending order—using price crossing a deviation threshold as the direction sensor when impact is unknown (e.g. speeches).
data_needed: Pre-event mid/ask/bid; myDeviation in points; paired buy-stop/sell-stop; OnTrade hook to cancel opposite
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD around NFP example; stop deviation in pips; session-expiring pendings
why_new_for_mis: Supplies a nonparametric regime-change trigger: the first stop fill is a live breakout-commitment bit usable when forecast/impact labels are missing.
quote: Stop orders help avoid these fake-outs by ensuring that the trade only triggers when the market commits to a direction beyond a specific price point.

idea_name: Post-fill slippage as news-execution quality sensor
mechanism: After a stop fills, SlippageReduction recomputes intended SL/TP from actual open vs expected open (slip = (actual−expected)/Point) and PositionModify to restore planned R:R—treating fill displacement during news as measurable adverse excursion from volatility/liquidity stress.
data_needed: Expected open from SetBuyStop/SetSellStop; actual POSITION_PRICE_OPEN; planned SL/TP distances; comment/magic filter
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD NFP example: expected 1.13118 vs fill 1.13134 → 16-point slip; 1:6 R:R case
why_new_for_mis: Converts news-window fill gap into an online volatility/liquidity stress reading MIS can log per event id.
quote: Due to the volatility of the NFP event the buy trade is executed at an unfavorable price of 1.13134 ... Slippage: (1.13134 - 1.13118)/0.00001 -> 16 pips

mechanism: When ImpactRequired, SQL ranks historical same-EventId rows in the prior 24 months whose Forecast≷Prevalue direction matches the current event’s Forecast≷Prevalue, takes DateOrder=1 (most recent analog), and copies that past EVENTIMPACT onto today’s and the next event—sensing expected directional impulse without the live print.
data_needed: MQL5Calendar with Forecast, Prevalue, EventImpact, EventId, DST schedule columns; in-memory daily+next-event query
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multi-currency MQL5 economic calendar; 24-month lookback; +60-day next-event horizon; traded via event currency vs profit currency
why_new_for_mis: Builds an event-impact sensor from analogical surprise direction—MIS can score upcoming releases by nearest historical twin before actuals land.
quote: It looks for previous events within the last 24 months where both forecast and prevalue are available and compares them to the current event. If the forecast value is larger than the prevalue (or vice versa) or even equal, it matches this with the historical event having the same trend ... and assigns its impact to the current event.

idea_name: Upcoming and recent event-date calendar views
mechanism: SQL views Upcoming Event Dates / Recent Event Dates take DISTINCT EventIds, attach next future (or last past) DST_NONE timestamp vs Record.Date, and emit weekday labels—exposing per-event recurrence timing as a first-class calendar feature for filtration and UI awareness.
data_needed: Persistent calendar DB tables MQL5Calendar, TimeSchedule, Record; views RecentEventInfo_View and UpcomingEventInfo_View
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Global calendar events (AU, NZ, JP, EU, etc.); day-of-week tagging; DST_NONE schedule
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a structured event-recurrence sensor (time-to-next / time-since-last per EventId) usable as exogenous regime context beyond raw price.
quote: new views will be added to present data such as displaying dates for the last news event or the next news event for each unique event in the MQL5 Economic calendar

series_key: overcoming the limitation of machine learning
mechanism: Fit identical Ridge models to ΔPrice, ΔMA_C, ΔStoch Main, ΔRSI over HORIZON; score each with mutual_info_regression(y_true, y_pred) on a held-out window; choose the target maximizing MI because MI is unitless, nonparametric, and zero-anchored—unlike RMSE which prefers mean-hugging low-scale targets.
data_needed: OHLC + MA O/H/L/C + RSI + Stoch Main/Signal CSV; horizon-shifted delta targets; sklearn mutual_info_regression; time-series holdout
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD PERIOD_CURRENT; HORIZON=10; ~3000 bars fetch; last 3y held out; TimeSeriesSplit(5, gap=HORIZON)
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a scale-free sensor of which labeled series a model can actually track—usable to auto-pick regime/vol proxies without trusting RMSE.
quote: when selecting between multiple targets to model, we recommend choosing the one that maximizes MI. ... MI is more robust and less vulnerable to such manipulation

series_key: overcoming the limitation of machine learning
mechanism: Among candidate deltas, ΔStoch Main uniquely produces out-of-sample predictions that span true test width (MI ≫ price/MA/RSI) instead of collapsing to the training mean; an MLPRegressor tuned by RandomizedSearchCV then forecasts Stoch Target 2, and long/short rules combine onnx_targets>0.5 with Stoch level/engulfing filters, ATR-scaled stops.
data_needed: Same 11 features; binary Stoch rise labels; ONNX MLP; daily new-bar inference; ATR(14) for exits
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; train excluding last 3y; backtest ~2022–2025 real ticks; daily decision bar; Stoch(5,3,3)
why_new_for_mis: Shows oscillator-change forecasts as a neural market-width/regime sensor that remains informative when direct ΔPrice models reward-hack to the mean.
quote: This model is the only one in our discussion that reasonably resembles the distribution of test observations and captures the market’s width better than the prior models.
